Going around the edge to (3,5) would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes down.
The line must go down: around the edge to (4,5) is number 9, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (1,2) would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would leave both number 7 and number 8 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Going left would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes down.

Going left would leave both cell (2,3) and cell (4,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
The line must go left: right is number 9, which comes later.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
